shouldFix.title: The D-096 clause names only the (A) leg and presents it as the operative remaining gate for DR-117; D-100 clause 3 forecloses DR-117 from that regime entirely.
shouldFix.subjectText: This artifact does not mint a D-096 (A) grant. Owner-recorded deferral of an inside-slice DR-117 obligation is blocked until a user-express D-096 (A) grant exists.
whatTheLiveBytesSay: D-096 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md line 3802) blocks owner-recording until BOTH '(A) an applicable owner grant covering every named role for the candidate being recorded and (B) separately D-000-reviewed condition-2 owner-recording mechanics'.
The (B) leg is ADOPTED at D-100 (line 3998), whose Readiness effect is 'Zero. D-096 (A) stays unsatisfied.' So for eligible candidates (A) is indeed the remaining gate.

But D-100's adopted turn-3 subject, clause 3, is titled 'The only eligible candidates' and enumerates the five D-096 artifacts; its precondition list requires 'the candidate is one of the five D-096 artifacts'. The rows covered are DR-106, DR-108, DR-109, DR-110, DR-113 and DR-116.
D-100's must-not list expressly bars 'Expand eligible rows beyond the five D-096 candidates.'
shouldFix.defect: Read strictly the sentence states a necessary condition and is not false. But its operative force in a contract whose stated job is to refuse a succession route is to identify the bar, and 'blocked until X exists' reads as 'X is what unblocks it.' For DR-117 a user-express (A) grant would NOT open owner-recorded deferral: the row is outside the D-096/D-100 eligibility set, and D-100 forbids expanding that set. The clause therefore understates the bar for the one row this artifact governs.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing is authorized by the misstatement. The artifact mints no grant, records no deferral, binds NOTHING, and the row stays OPEN. The error is in stating the bar, not in crossing it.
shouldFix.steelmanConsidered: That 'inside-slice DR-117 obligation' might mean some narrower obligation touching DR-117 rather than the row itself. Even on that reading the D-096/D-100 regime is keyed to the five named candidates, and the clause supplies no such limiting context.
shouldFix.repair: Name D-100 clause 3 and state that DR-117 is not one of the five eligible D-096 candidates, so no owner-recorded deferral route exists for this row under that regime at all — an (A) grant alone would not open one, and D-100 bars expanding the eligible set.
